steps.title: A coastal white
steps.body: Vermentino gives light to medium-bodied whites with lemon, grapefruit, green apple, white flowers, Mediterranean herbs and a saline, almond finish. Acidity is medium to high. It's at home by the sea, and its salty, herbal character is often linked to coastal winds and soils.

steps.title: Many names
steps.body: Vermentino probably spread around the western Mediterranean centuries ago. It's called Rolle in Provence and the Languedoc, Pigato in Liguria and Favorita in Piedmont; DNA shows they're the same grape. It likes heat, sun and drought, and tolerates poor, sandy or granite soils, typical of Mediterranean coasts.

steps.prompt: Match each name to its region.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale lemon colour, citrus and herbs like rosemary and thyme, a crisp palate and a slightly bitter, saline almond finish. Compared with Sauvignon Blanc, it's less pungent and green; compared with Pinot Grigio, more herbal and saline.

steps.prompt: Rolle and Vermentino are the same grape.
steps.explanation: Yes. Rolle is its name in Provence and the Languedoc.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Vermentino gives citrus, herbs and a saline finish
It's Rolle in Provence, Pigato in Liguria, Favorita in Piedmont
It loves heat, sun and coastal soils
